title: EFE Robot MCP tools, v0
description: Canonical, un-narrowed tool definitions. The server narrows enums and bounds per robot (schema.py). Every inputSchema is a self-contained draft 2020-12 object schema without $ref or top-level combinators, so every harness accepts it as a function definition.

conventions.frame: the robot base at the start of the call: +X forward, +Y left, +Z up

tools.name: describe_robot
tools.description: The robot: its parts (arms, hands, grippers, base, legs) and what each accepts, joint names and limits, cameras, control rate, the action spaces, the conventions and the time left. Call this first.

tools.name: observe
tools.description: Current camera images and robot state. Images, depth and video are written to files in the workspace; the result has their paths plus camera intrinsics and extrinsics, simulated time, time left and each part's joints, gripper and end-effector pose (robot base frame). With seconds > 0 the robot holds its last command while the scene runs for that long, and a video is saved.

cameras.description: camera names (default: the robot's default cameras)

depth.description: also save a depth map per camera that has one (.npy, float32 metres, 0 = no reading); cameras without depth are listed in no_depth_cameras

seconds.description: hold and watch for this long (0: no time passes)

inline_cameras.description: cameras to also return as small low-resolution images in the result

tools.name: move_robot
tools.description: Move one or more parts to goals and block until done. A part goal sets an end-effector pose (position + quaternion_wxyz in the robot base frame at the start of the call), joint positions, and/or the gripper (0 open, 1 closed). A base goal {target: "base", dx, dy, dyaw} moves a mobile base by that much in its own frame. Parts not listed hold still. Returns whether it moved, which goals were reached (with errors), a failure category, the time left and the paths of the frames saved after the move.

target.description: a part of this robot, or base

quaternion_wxyz.description: end-effector orientation (w, x, y, z), robot base frame

joint_positions.description: absolute joint targets in the part's joint order

duration_s.description: how long the motion takes (default: from the distance at a moderate speed)

collision_aware.description: plan around obstacles where the robot's controller can (otherwise ignored, and the result says so)

tools.name: locomote
tools.description: Walk or drive with the robot's own locomotion controller: body-frame velocity (vx forward m/s, vy left m/s, wz counter-clockwise rad/s) for duration_s, then stop. Blocks until done.

height.description: body or pelvis height command (m), where the controller takes one

tools.name: execute_trajectory
tools.description: Execute a dense trajectory, rows dt seconds apart, and block until done. space joint / ee / ee_delta / whole_body: `rows` is a list of objects naming parts, e.g. {"left": {"joint_positions": [...], "gripper": 1}} (joint), {"left": {"position": [...], "quaternion_wxyz": [...]}} (ee, robot base frame at the start of the call), {"arm": {"dpos": [...], "drot": [...]}} (ee_delta: per-row translation and rotation vector), {"base": {"vx": .., "vy": .., "wz": ..}} (whole_body); parts a row does not name hold. space native: `native_rows` are number arrays in one of the robot's own action types (`action_type`, see describe_robot), sent unchanged. A long trajectory can come from a file under /app (`rows_file`: .json list of rows, or .npy / .csv of native rows).

rows_file.description: path under /app of a .json, .npy or .csv file of rows

action_type.description: space native: the robot's action type

dt.description: seconds between rows (default: the control period)

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Hold the current command and let `seconds` of time pass (0 = none); with `operation`, first wait for an operation a previous call left pending. Returns the state afterwards and the paths of saved frames.

tools.name: signal
tools.description: End the episode or talk to the operator: done (the job is done), infeasible (it cannot be done), ask_operator (a question; the answer comes back), report (tell the operator something). The note says what and why.

category.description: report: the category, where the robot defines them

tools.name: reset_episode
tools.description: Start a new episode from the same frozen starting state (robot and every object back where they started), where this robot allows resets: it abandons the running episode, uses one reset of the budget (describe_robot: resets_left) and takes no simulated time. Returns the new episode's state and the paths of its frames.
